correctness.rationale: Radial/child-antisymmetric decomposition diagonalizes the full tree adjacency into Jacobi blocks of lengths 1..L+1 and yields distinct eigenvalue count D(L)=sum_{r=2}^{L+2}phi(r). Leaf transitivity and backward leaf eigenvector induction show every eigenvalue has a nonzero single-leaf projection. For two leaves splitting h levels above, eigenvalues absent from their common child-subtree force equal leaf projections; eigenvalues of that subtree yield two independent projections by using a third branch, requiring b>=3. Hence bright rank D(L)+D(h-1). Orthogonal dark/bright splitting and strictly negative real parts of the dissipative generator on bright space establish eventual capture for positive losses; strict totient increments establish optimal far-apart placement. Independently obtained modular Krylov ranks for b=3,4 and a boundary contradiction for b=2.
residual_risks: Modular finite ranks do not prove all L; b=2 counterexample shows b>=3 sharp. Capture is total integrated eventual loss, not capture times; requires adjacency unit hopping and positive rates.
